3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: It was a beautiful, sunny day in Pales.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: From within the courtyard of Castle Reinhart, near the front gate, I admired the fortress's timeless grandeur.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Most of the city center was prepared for the Victory Parade. Everything seemed clean, as if the war had never happened.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: However, if anyone went into the back alleys, to government buildings, to residential areas, one would find sandbags lying around and bullet holes on the walls.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Nothing that couldn't be fixed in due time.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: I wondered if I should have it renamed.

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: The gates creaked open with a heavy groan, and I spurred my horse, following the parade.

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: The marching band started their song. Loud cheers rose from the crowds all around me as I slowly made my way through the capital.

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: A child tried to approach my horse with a bouquet of roses. The Golden Guard held her back.

17.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
17.text: Gesture for her to approach and take the bouquet.

18.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
18.text: Disregard her and follow the protocol.

19.speaker: Narrator

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: An old man from the crowd tried to approach my horse with what looked like a cane. He was swinging it over his head, swearing and cursing.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Multiple guards immediately jumped on him and held him on the ground. The crowd looked disturbed and curious about what would happen.

25.speaker: Player_Romus
25.text: "He's just an old man. Let him go. What is he even going to do?"

26.speaker: Player_Romus
26.text: "Straight to prison. Make sure he learns his place."

27.speaker: Narrator
27.text: Titus looked towards me for orders.

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: The guards let him go. He cursed and disappeared into the crowd.

36.speaker: Narrator

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: Rizian airplanes flew very close to the ground, deafening everyone.

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: What a shame it was to not have the pride of our navy, our flagship.

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: The Rizian fleet was covering the entirety of the Gulf of Pales, leaving no space for any other vessel.

74.speaker: Narrator
74.text: Each battleship deck was full of marines. I could see them saluting from a distance.

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: I could see the marines saluting from a distance.

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: The parade finally stopped and I got off my horse. I patted him on the back.

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: In celebration, battleships cannons fired into the air.

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: In front of me, on the grand stairs to my new palace, was Duke Reinhart. Behind him was the Throne of Pales. He was kneeling and looking at the ground.

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: A half-burned Palesian flag landed on my foot. The wind must have brought it to me.

83.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
83.text: Pick it up and handle it with care and honor.

85.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
85.text: Rip it up in front of the crowd.

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: I approached the defeated man before me.

88.speaker: Axel Reinhart
88.text: "That's it, Your Majesty. You've won. Pales surrenders."
88.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_PrimeMinister_Daria"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_PrimeMinister_Manus"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_PrimeMinister_Adarfo"] == true) == false)

89.speaker: Player_Romus
89.text: "I won't be satisfied until you get down and lick my boots."

90.speaker: Narrator
90.text: He took the crown from his head and presented it to me.

91.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
91.text: Put the crown on your head.

93.speaker: Axel Reinhart
93.text: "I hope that you are satisfied. I have nothing else to say to you."

94.speaker: Player_Romus
94.text: "Apologize to your King. In front of everyone."

96.speaker: Player_Romus
96.text: "I hope you enjoy your time in prison."

98.speaker: Axel Reinhart
98.text: "What? That's ridiculous. We're both gentlemen here--"

99.speaker: Narrator
99.text: The guards grabbed him and made him kneel down further.

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: I smiled as he reluctantly stuck his tongue out and licked my boot.

102.speaker: Narrator
102.text: The guards grabbed him and made him kneel down further.

105.speaker: Narrator
105.text: The guards grabbed him and made him kneel down further.

108.speaker: Axel Reinhart
108.text: "The Grand Duchy is all yours now."

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: The guards roughly pushed Axel and he fell to the ground. I watched as he was dragged away.
111.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_PrimeMinister_Daria"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_PrimeMinister_Manus"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_PrimeMinister_Adarfo"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_Success"] == true) == false)

112.speaker: Narrator

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: I turned around and looked at Pales.

114.speaker: Narrator
114.text: The rays of sun were coming down from the clouds to paint the rooftops golden.

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: I sat down on the Throne of Pales.

123.speaker: Player_Romus
123.text: "Have you heard of a device called 'Saint Mercy'? We haven't used it since last century. But we're going to break it out of retirement especially for you."

125.speaker: Narrator
125.text: My eyes caught Major Tigris -- now Colonel -- in front of the column.

160.speaker: Narrator
160.text: Manus Sazon led the provincial troops from Brenas. He looked much older and more hardened than the last time I'd seen him.

165.text: After returning from the front, the first thing he'd done was request Vina's hand in marriage.

166.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
166.text: Now that he'd proven himself, it was finally time.

179.speaker: Player_Romus
179.text: "Much appreciated. Guards, arrest this man for his many, many violent acts against Rizia."

180.speaker: Player_Romus
180.text: "I will. Guards, arrest this man for his many, many violent acts against Rizia."

182.speaker: Player_Romus
182.text: "You are a war criminal and you must be treated appropriately."

183.speaker: Player_Romus
183.text: "As you walk free today, remember the mercy King Romus Toras showed you. It is more than you deserve."

184.speaker: Player_Romus
184.text: "You have done what any monarch would in your situation. You have my blessing to leave."

188.speaker: Player_Romus
188.text: "One more thing. I want him tortured. The so-called Duke will beg for his life."

191.speaker: Player_Romus
191.text: "You will stay there until you have repented for your infringement on my kingdom's sovereignty."

192.speaker: Axel Reinhart
192.text: "I swear to you, I've repented already--"

195.speaker: Narrator
195.text: He bowed low to the ground.

196.speaker: Axel Reinhart
196.text: "Thank you, Your Majesty. I will not forget this."

218.speaker: Narrator

219.speaker: Daria de Rava

220.speaker: Narrator

221.speaker: Player_Romus
221.text: "A reminder of why we keep fighting for Rizia’s future."

222.speaker: Player_Romus
222.text: "A parade is just a show. The real work remains ahead."

223.speaker: Player_Romus
223.text: "This is a celebration of those who earned victory, not merely observed it."

227.speaker: Player_Romus
227.text: "Ah, yes, the skies. Always so supportive in matters of war and statecraft."

231.speaker: Player_Romus
231.text: "Yes, the heavens themselves seem to honor the sacrifices made for this victory."

232.speaker: Narrator
232.text: Daria’s smile faltered, but she quickly regained her composure.

235.speaker: Daria de Rava
235.text: "Indeed, Your Majesty. But even victories deserve a moment in the sun."

236.speaker: Daria de Rava
236.text: "The skies were certainly kind to us in this war. Our brave air force helped save the day."

251.text: "Parades like this mask the true cost of war, glossing over the sacrifices of the working class who fought and died."

252.speaker: Player_Romus
252.text: "Perhaps, but even the working class needs to see that their sacrifices weren't in vain."

255.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
255.text: "Agreed. Those who bled for this victory must reap the rewards, not just the privileged few."

274.speaker: Narrator
274.text: Manus' smile faltered, but he quickly regained his composure.

275.speaker: Narrator
275.text: Adarfo’s gaze hardened before slowly turning away.

276.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
276.text: Allow the Prime Minister to go ahead of you.

310.speaker: Axel Reinhart

311.speaker: Player_Romus
311.text: "Ah, of course. My apologies. I got ahead of myself there."

312.speaker: Player_Romus
312.text: "Damned rules and their constraints! But fine. I'll allow it to stand, for now."

316.speaker: Player_Romus
316.text: "I'm sorry for everything that happened. But trust me, this is for the best."

366.speaker: Narrator
366.text: He'd returned from the front only to find his home province in Crown hands, his family in disarray and the House of Delegates dismantled.

370.speaker: Narrator
370.text: He'd returned from the front only to find his home province in Crown hands and his family in disarray.

371.speaker: Narrator
371.text: I almost felt bad for him.

372.speaker: Narrator
372.text: Rows of polished medals gleamed across his chest, their ribbons crisp and colors sharp against the dark fabric of his uniform.
